subject: physics
question_text: State the number of significant figures in the following: a) 6729  b) 0.024  c) 0.08240  d) 6.032  e) 4.57 × 10⁸

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The rules used
lines: Zeros before the first non-zero digit are not
significant. Zeros after it are significant.
In a × 10ⁿ form only the digits of a count.
steps.why: A leading zero only places the decimal point, so it carries no information about the measurement. A trailing zero was actually read off the instrument, so it does.
common_mistakes: Counting the leading zeros in 0.024 and calling it four significant figures.

recall.must_convey: That leading zeros are not significant, trailing zeros after a non-zero digit are, and in scientific notation only the digits of the number count.
accept: only the digits before the power

steps.memory_tip: Leading zeros only place the point. Trailing zeros were really measured.
steps.margin_note: One rule line covers all five parts.

steps.label: The five answers
steps.why: In 0.08240 the two leading zeros do not count but the final zero does, which is why it is four and not three or six.
common_mistakes: Counting the power of ten in 4.57 × 10⁸ as extra significant figures.

recall.must_convey: That the answers are four, two, four, four and three.

steps.memory_tip: 0.08240 is the tricky one: leading zeros out, the last zero in — four.
steps.margin_note: Write all five. Each one is quick.

insider_note: Five sub-parts, two marks. Write the rule once, then answer all five — do not spend the space explaining each one.
